explanation: Quinine comes from the bark of the South American cinchona tree. It glows bright blue under ultraviolet light, so tonic water shines under a black light.

claims.text: Tonic water's bitter taste is due to quinine, a compound once widely used to treat and prevent malaria.
Caffeine, tannin and theobromine are not what gives tonic water its bitterness.
Quinine is obtained from the bark of the cinchona tree, native to South America.
Quinine fluoresces blue under ultraviolet light, so tonic water glows under a black light.
